sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Ketrowa.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·凯特罗娃。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: All right, this morning changes are coming to some of your favorite snacks.
sentences.zh: 好的，今天早上，你们最喜欢的一些零食将迎来改变。

sentences.en: This summer, some of the biggest food companies in America have announced that they're planning to stop using artificial food dyes.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，美国一些最大的食品公司宣布，他们计划停止使用人工食用色素。

sentences.en: It's not just one company making this big announcement.
sentences.zh: 做出这一重大宣布的不仅仅是一家公司。

sentences.en: Kraft Heinz, one of the nation's largest food companies,
sentences.zh: 卡夫亨氏，全美最大的食品公司之一，

sentences.en: General Mills is the maker of cereals, including Cinnamon Toast Crunch.
sentences.zh: 通用磨坊是各种谷物的制造商，包括肉桂吐司脆片。

sentences.en: Iconic products like Kool-Aid and Jell-O, poised for a new look.
sentences.zh: 酷爱饮品和果冻等标志性产品，正准备以崭新的面貌示人。

sentences.en: Dozens of the top ice cream makers have agreed.
sentences.zh: 数十家顶尖冰淇淋制造商已经同意了。

sentences.en: It's also those jet-popped marshmallows, as well as...
sentences.zh: 还有那些喷射膨化棉花糖，以及……

sentences.en: It's a move that would transform the look of some of the most iconic brands that we buy.
sentences.zh: 这一举措将彻底改变我们购买的一些最具标志性品牌的外观。

sentences.en: Everyone is saying we just don't need these artificial dyes anymore.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说，我们真的不再需要这些人工色素了。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Julie Cresswell on how the health secretary, Robert F.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事朱莉·克雷斯韦尔将探讨卫生部长小罗伯特·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy Jr., got Big Food to commit to a change it resisted for years and that could be bad for business.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪如何让大型食品公司承诺做出他们抵制了多年、且可能对业务不利的改变。

sentences.en: It's Monday, July 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月28日，星期一。

sentences.en: Julie, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 朱莉，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: This is your first time on The Daily, right?
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次上《每日新闻》，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm so excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: We're excited to have you.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: So you cover the food industry, which with RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 所以你负责报道食品行业，而随着小RFK

sentences.en: now overseeing the Food and Drug Administration is facing a lot of potential change.
sentences.zh: 现在主管食品药品监督管理局，该行业正面临许多潜在的变革。

sentences.en: And we saw our first major example of that recently when these big food companies came out and said they are going to eliminate artificial dyes from their products.
sentences.zh: 我们最近看到了这方面的第一个重大例子，当时这些大型食品公司站出来宣布他们将从产品中消除人工色素。

sentences.en: How big of a deal are these announcements?
sentences.zh: 这些声明有多大分量？

sentences.en: Just put this into context for me.
sentences.zh: 请为我把这放在宏观背景下看看。

sentences.en: This is, for the American food system, one of the biggest changes we've seen in decades, period.
sentences.zh: 对美国食品系统而言，这是几十年来最大、最彻底的变革之一。

sentences.en: No other administration, Republican, Democrat, has gotten the food industry to agree en masse to sort of make a significant change like this ever.
sentences.zh: 没有任何其他政府（无论是共和党还是民主党）曾让食品行业大规模同意做出这样重大的改变。

sentences.en: If this works, this administration and Kennedy actually do have the opportunity to really reshape the American food system.
sentences.zh: 如果这招管用，本届政府和肯尼迪确实有机会真正重塑美国的食品系统。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, he famously says he wants to make America healthy again.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他那句名言是想让美国再次健康。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Where does his war on these artificial dyes fit in with that?
sentences.zh: 他对这些人造色素的口水战是如何契这一点的？

sentences.en: He sees artificial dyes as part of the bigger picture around chronic disease.
sentences.zh: 他将人工色素视为慢性病这个宏大画面的一部分。

sentences.en: The whole issue with artificial dyes is they sort of fall in that spectrum of processed foods in America that he sees as not good for Americans and particularly American youth.
sentences.zh: 关于人工色素的整个问题在于，它们大致属于美国加工食品的范畴，在他看来，这对美国人特别是美国青少年没有好处。

sentences.en: But this idea of making American healthy again, and especially by going after artificial dyes, is not new.
sentences.zh: 但这种让美国再次健康的想法，尤其是通过打击人工色素的想法，并不是什么新主意。

sentences.en: Vani and I are both food bloggers, and she does investigations.
sentences.zh: 瓦妮和我都是美食博主，她会做调查。

sentences.en: And we were just alarmed by what we uncovered.
sentences.zh: 我们对我们所揭露的事情感到震惊。

sentences.en: Basically, these companies, these are American...
sentences.zh: 基本上，这些公司，这些都是美国的……

sentences.en: You've had a lot of these momfluencers and people within the movement that have been focusing on artificial dyes going back at least a decade.
sentences.zh: 你们有许多这样的“妈妈网红”和运动内部人士，他们至少在过去十年里一直专注于人工色素。

sentences.en: I'm here for all Americans who don't know the truth about our food industry.
sentences.zh: 我在这里是为了所有不知道我们食品行业真相的美国人。

sentences.en: So I started a petition.
sentences.zh: 所以我发起了一份请愿书。

sentences.en: Having petitions signed by people and taking it to Kellogg's and taking it to Mars and trying to pressure them to remove artificial dyes.
sentences.zh: 让人们签署请愿书，并把它带到家乐氏和玛氏，试图向他们施压，要求他们去除人工色素。

sentences.en: And what were the arguments they were making about why this should happen?
sentences.zh: 他们当时提出的支持这样做的理由是什么？

sentences.en: You know, there was a number of arguments that they were making.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们提出了很多理由。

sentences.en: So what is wrong with artificial food dyes?
sentences.zh: 那么人造食用色素有什么问题呢？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, they're made in a laboratory with chemicals derived from petroleum.
sentences.zh: 首先，它们是在实验室里用从石油中提取的化学物质制成的。

sentences.en: One is these are dyes that are made from petroleum.
sentences.zh: 一是这些染料是从石油中提取的。

sentences.en: The same type of ingredients like gasoline, asphalt, and tar.
sentences.zh: 与汽油、沥青和焦油属于同类型的成分。

sentences.en: They're not from natural ingredients at all.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不是天然成分。

sentences.en: A second argument is, you know, these dyes are used largely in foods that are geared and marketed towards children.
sentences.zh: 第二个论点是，你知道，这些色素很大程度上用于针对儿童销售和营销的食品中。

sentences.en: And they produce bogus studies that say these food dyes are healthy because their marketing survey says that the neon colors make kids want to buy it.
sentences.zh: 他们炮制出虚假的虚假研究，说这些食用色素是健康的，因为他们的营销调研显示，霓虹色彩会让孩子们想买它。

sentences.en: You know, adults aren't sitting down to a big old bowl of Froot Loops.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，成年人可不会坐下来吃一大碗水果圈。

sentences.en: You know, it's geared to make children.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是为了迎合儿童设计的。

sentences.en: Speak for yourself, Julie.
sentences.zh: 请别把我算进去，朱莉。

sentences.en: Well, we've all been there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们都经历过。

sentences.en: But yeah, these are food that children want to eat because they're bright, they're colorful, they're fun.
sentences.zh: 但是是的，这些是孩子们想吃的食物，因为它们明亮、色彩斑斓、很有趣。

sentences.en: And, you know, marketing executives inside all these companies know that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所有这些公司内部的营销高管都心知肚明。

sentences.en: But one of the strongest arguments lodged against these artificial food dyes really has to do with the health implications of kids consuming them in large amounts.
sentences.zh: 但针对这些人工食用色素的最强有力的论据之一，实际上与儿童大量摄入这些色素对健康的危害有关。

sentences.en: Artificial food dyes have been proven to increase hyperactivity in children to negatively affect...
sentences.zh: 事实证明，人工食用色素会加剧儿童的多动症，对……产生负面影响。

sentences.en: And those concerns have been echoed more recently by RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 小RFK最近也呼应了这些担忧。

sentences.en: It's very clear that dyes, all of them, are linked in very, very strong studies to ADHD.
sentences.zh: 很明显，所有这些染料都在非常强有力的研究中与多动症联系在一起。

sentences.en: And are those claims actually true, Julie?
sentences.zh: 朱莉，这些说法真的属实吗？

sentences.en: Like, what do we know about the science there, about the evidence?
sentences.zh: 比如说，关于那里的科学，关于证据，我们都知道些什么？

sentences.en: There's not a huge body of evidence.
sentences.zh: 并没有大量的证据。

sentences.en: and there's been no research showing a causal relationship between food dyes and ADHD.
sentences.zh: 而且也没有研究表明食用色素与多动症之间存在因果关系。

sentences.en: There was one study, though, that did start to get a lot of attention and helped kind of kick off this push against artificial dyes.
sentences.zh: 不过，确实有一项研究开始受到广泛关注，并帮助引发了这场反对人工色素的运动。

sentences.en: You know, that occurs around 2007 in the UK when they do something called the Southampton study.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那大约发生在2007年的英国，当时他们做了一项名为南安普顿的研究。

sentences.en: Basically, they started giving children drinks.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们开始给儿童喝饮料。

sentences.en: Some had artificial colors in them and then another group that didn't.
sentences.zh: 有些里面含有人工色素，另一组则没有。

sentences.en: And they sort of watched their behavior.
sentences.zh: 然后他们观察他们的行为。

sentences.en: And the children that were given the drinks with red 40 or other artificial colors in them started showing more hyperactive behavior than the others.
sentences.zh: 喝了含有红色40号或其他人工色素饮料的儿童，比其他人表现出更多的好动行为。

sentences.en: And that's what ultimately led the European Union to take sort of a tougher stance or a harder look at these artificial colors.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点最终导致欧盟对这些人工色素采取了更强硬的立场或进行了更严格的审视。

sentences.en: And so in the EU, when you say they started to take a harder stance, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 所以在欧盟，当你说他们开始采取更强硬的立场时，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: What did they do?
sentences.zh: 他们做了什么？

sentences.en: So one of the things the European Union did is in 2010, they started putting warning labels on foods and beverages and snacks that had these certain,
sentences.zh: 所以欧盟做的一件事是，在2010年，他们开始在含有这些特定成分的食品、饮料和零食上贴上警告标签，

sentences.en: they call them the Southampton Six.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“南安普顿六人组”。

sentences.en: It's six specific artificial dyes that they believe are linked to behavioral issues.
sentences.zh: 这是六种他们认为与行为问题有关的特定人工色素。

sentences.en: And now if you buy a packet of candy that is made or contains one of these Southampton 6 artificial dyes,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你买一包糖果，里面含有或使用了这六种南安普顿人工色素之一，

sentences.en: they have a warning label on it that says something to the effect of this product could cause behavioral issues with children.
sentences.zh: 它们上面就会有一个警告标签，大意是本产品可能会引起儿童的行为问题。

sentences.en: Besides the warning labels on certain foods, you know,
sentences.zh: 除了某些食品上的警告标签，你知道，

sentences.en: there are certain artificial colors like red 3 that have either been banned or severely restricted in other countries because of their links to possible carcinogen and cancer in male rats.
sentences.zh: 某些人工色素（如红色3号）由于与雄性大鼠可能致癌的联系，在其他国家已被禁止或受到严格限制。

sentences.en: In fact, the evidence linking red dye 3 to cancer was compelling enough that the EU banned it back in the early 1990s.
sentences.zh: 事实上，将红色3号染料与癌症联系起来的证据非常有说服力，以至于欧盟早在20世纪90年代初就禁止了它。

sentences.en: But in the U.S., it took us much longer.
sentences.zh: 但在美国，我们花了很长时间。

sentences.en: The FDA just this year passed a ban on Red 3, and it doesn't go into effect until 2027.
sentences.zh: 美国食品药品监督管理局就在今年通过了对红色3号的禁令，直到2027年才会生效。

sentences.en: So it sounds like even though the body of evidence itself isn't entirely conclusive or as robust as it could be, you're saying there's these other countries that are taking
sentences.zh: 听起来，尽管证据本身并不完全确凿，也没有想象中那么充分，但你是在说其他国家正在采取

sentences.en: a much more aggressive stance on this.
sentences.zh: 更加激进的立场。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why hasn't the U.S.
sentences.zh: 为什么美国

sentences.en: gone that route?
sentences.zh: 没有走这条路？

sentences.en: The EU takes an approach with regulation is sort of like what's best for the consumer.
sentences.zh: 欧盟在监管方面采取的方法有点像对消费者最有利的方式。

sentences.en: So if you're introducing a new ingredient in Europe, let's say the European Union, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你要在欧洲（比如欧盟）推出一种新成分，你知道，

sentences.en: you're going to have to produce a bunch of scientific documents and papers and research that basically says, you know,
sentences.zh: 你必须出具大量科学文件、论文和研究，基本上证明，你知道，

sentences.en: that this ingredient is not going to cause harm to the consumer.
sentences.zh: 这种成分不会对消费者造成伤害。

sentences.en: And then the European regulators are going to weigh about that.
sentences.zh: 然后欧盟的监管机构会对此进行权衡。

sentences.en: They're going to think about that before any new ingredient gets introduced there.
sentences.zh: 在任何新成分在那里推出之前，他们都会仔细考虑这一点。

sentences.en: It's something called the precautionary principle.
sentences.zh: 这被称为预防原则。

sentences.en: Here in the United States, we tend to take sort of more of a what's good for industry approach.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们往往采取对行业有利的方法。

sentences.en: Big food here is a very powerful force, you know, very powerful lobbying.
sentences.zh: 这里的大型食品企业是一股非常强大的力量，你知道，游说力量非常强大。

sentences.en: They've got their people that have been in and out of the FDA.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的人进出食品药品监督管理局。

sentences.en: They put their people on research groups and boards.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己的人安插在研究小组和董事会里。

sentences.en: And so I think the regulatory framework and the ability for companies to introduce new ingredients, at least, is a little looser.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为监管框架以及公司推出新成分的能力至少要宽松一些。

sentences.en: There's a little bit more self-regulation, a little bit more trust me built into the system here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国的体制内多了一点自我监管，多了一点信任。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But American food companies have taken steps in the past to remove artificial colors from their foods.
sentences.zh: 但美国食品公司过去曾采取措施从食品中去除人工色素。

sentences.en: And basically, it was a buSt. Why?
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一次彻底的失败。为什么？

sentences.en: So back in 2015, there was a movement here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 早在2015年，美国就兴起了一场运动。

sentences.en: Again, a little bit of writing off of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也是在一定程度上效仿欧盟。

sentences.en: You had a push to get big food to change its ways, to dump some of these artificial colors.
sentences.zh: 当时有一股推动力，要求大型食品公司改变做法，抛弃其中一些人工色素。

sentences.en: Fruity Trix.
sentences.zh: 果味趣奇。

sentences.en: Trix.
sentences.zh: 趣奇。

sentences.en: And so at the time, you had companies like General Mills, which makes Trix breakfast cereal.
sentences.zh: 因此，当时你拥有像通用磨坊这样的公司，它生产趣奇早餐麦片。

sentences.en: General Mills announcing it will phase out artificial colors.
sentences.zh: 通用磨坊宣布将逐步淘汰人工色素。

sentences.en: Come out with products that had no artificial colors.
sentences.zh: 推出不含人工色素的产品。

sentences.en: General Mills could not find good alternatives for blue and green pieces in his Trix cereal, so the company is getting rid of those colors.
sentences.zh: 通用磨坊无法为其趣奇麦片中的蓝色和绿色颗粒找到好的替代品，因此该公司正在取消这些颜色。

sentences.en: Other colors, such as red, won't be as vibrant.
sentences.zh: 其他颜色，比如红色，也不会那么鲜艳。

sentences.en: And people didn't really want it.
sentences.zh: 而人们其实并不买账。

sentences.en: General Mills says customers have been asking for the old formula to come back.
sentences.zh: 通用磨坊表示，顾客一直在要求恢复旧配方。

sentences.en: Consumers were writing in saying that the new colors made them depressed.
sentences.zh: 消费者写信说，新颜色让他们感到沮丧。

sentences.en: So what do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以你怎么看？

sentences.en: Do you think it was the kids or the adults complaining about Trix?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是小孩子还是大人在抱怨趣奇麦片？

sentences.en: Probably the grown-ups.
sentences.zh: 可能是成年人吧。

sentences.en: They didn't want to eat this cereal.
sentences.zh: 他们不想吃这种麦片。

sentences.en: A cereal company is bringing its old-school cereal back.
sentences.zh: 一家麦片公司正在把它的复古麦片带回来。

sentences.en: General Mills' Trix cereal will once again be made with artificial dyes and flavors.
sentences.zh: 通用磨坊的趣奇麦片将再次使用人工色素和香精制造。

sentences.en: And Mars, big candy company Mars, it does some consumer analysis.
sentences.zh: 玛氏，大型糖果公司玛氏，做了一些消费者分析。

sentences.en: And basically,
sentences.zh: 基本上，

sentences.en: its conclusion from looking at and talking to consumers is that people in the EU were much more willing and actually wanted to have artificial colors taken out of their candy there.
sentences.zh: 它通过观察和与消费者交谈得出的结论是，欧盟的人们更愿意而且确实希望将糖果中的人工色素去除。

sentences.en: While people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而美国人

sentences.en: were like, do not touch my M&Ms.
sentences.zh: 则觉得：别碰我的M&M豆。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Don't mute my reds.
sentences.zh: 别把我的红色调暗。

sentences.en: Don't make me.
sentences.zh: 别逼我。

sentences.en: You know, take away my blue M&Ms, you know, without a doubt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，毫无疑问，把我的蓝色M&M豆拿走吧。

sentences.en: And so they reached a conclusion that after doing this research, that they weren't going to touch M&Ms and other, you know, bright treats and candies
sentences.zh: 因此他们得出一个结论，在做了这项研究后，他们不会动M&M豆以及其他你懂的、颜色鲜艳的零食和糖果，

sentences.en: that Americans wanted to have remain the same.
sentences.zh: 因为美国人希望它们保持原样。

sentences.en: It sounds like taking the dyes out of food, according to the companies, would probably reduce their sales.
sentences.zh: 听起来，根据这些公司的说法，从食物中去除色素可能会减少他们的销量。

sentences.en: Companies say, we've tried this.
sentences.zh: 食品公司说，我们试过了。

sentences.en: It didn't work.
sentences.zh: 行不通。

sentences.en: Generally speaking, yes.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，是的。

sentences.en: What's the conclusion that the companies draw about why Americans are, you know, less into the natural muted look of food?
sentences.zh: 关于为什么美国人，你知道的，不太喜欢食物那种天然的、柔和的外观，这些公司得出了什么结论？

sentences.en: There's a whole ton of like sort of food science around colors and how people interpret them.
sentences.zh: 围绕颜色以及人们如何解读颜色，其实有很多像这样的食品科学。

sentences.en: You know, there's a saying that, you know, we eat with our eyes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，俗话说得好，我们是用眼睛吃饭的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: When you see a bright-colored chip or a bright-colored candy, your mind is telling sort of your palate, this is going to taste strong.
sentences.zh: 当你看到颜色鲜艳的薯片或颜色鲜艳的糖果时，你的大脑会向味蕾传达一种信息，这东西味道会很浓。

sentences.en: This is going to taste spicy.
sentences.zh: 这东西味道会很辣。

sentences.en: This is going to taste salty.
sentences.zh: 这东西味道会很咸。

sentences.en: You know, you have already in your head what that's going to taste like before you put it in your mouth.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在你把它放进嘴里之前，你的脑海里就已经知道它会是什么味道了。

sentences.en: And I think so American food companies are trying to figure out where that balance is because they've got decades of background and research that say bright-colored cell.
sentences.zh: 所以我想美国食品公司正在努力找出平衡点，因为他们有几十年的背景和研究表明，颜色鲜艳好卖。

sentences.en: And sales are just one part of the concern inside these companies.
sentences.zh: 而销量只是这些公司内部顾虑的一部分。

sentences.en: The other part of the concern is expenses.
sentences.zh: 另一部分的顾虑是成本。

sentences.en: You know, the long and short of it is moving away from artificial colors, which are really inexpensive.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，简而言之，就是放弃人工合成色素，那些东西真的很便宜。

sentences.en: That is going to drive the costs up for the company.
sentences.zh: 这会推高公司的成本。

sentences.en: You know, and then one of the biggest issues for food companies right now is matching those colors.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，目前食品公司最大的问题之一就是调配这些颜色。

sentences.en: You know, what we've created in America using artificial colors is a palette of colors.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们在美国用人工色素创造出来的，是一个颜色调色板。

sentences.en: that just don't exist in nature.
sentences.zh: 那些在自然界中根本不存在。

sentences.en: Blue, oh, really tough for food manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 蓝色，哦，对食品制造商来说太难了。

sentences.en: You know, a blueberry, which everybody's like, oh, we've got blueberries.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，蓝莓，每个人都觉得，哦，我们有蓝莓。

sentences.en: When you squish a blueberry, it's red.
sentences.zh: 当你把蓝莓捏碎时，它是红色的。

sentences.en: It's not blue.
sentences.zh: 它不是蓝色的。

sentences.en: Even greens, you're like, oh, we've got kale, we've got spinach.
sentences.zh: 甚至连绿色也是，你会觉得，哦，我们有羽衣甘蓝，我们有菠菜。

sentences.en: Yes, there are greens that occur in nature, but those greens are very tricky to deal with.
sentences.zh: 是的，自然界中确实存在绿色，但那些绿色非常难处理。

sentences.en: They degrade very, very quickly, very easily.
sentences.zh: 它们降解得非常、非常快，非常容易。

sentences.en: One of the issues with natural colors is they're very sensitive to heat and light.
sentences.zh: 天然色素的问题之一是它们对热和光非常敏感。

sentences.en: Think of your Gatorade in a clear bottle.
sentences.zh: 想想你装在透明瓶子里的佳得乐。

sentences.en: One of my kids loves the blue Gatorade in a clear bottle.
sentences.zh: 我的一个孩子喜欢透明瓶装的蓝色佳得乐。

sentences.en: If you switch to natural colors, you may have to, one, switch your packaging.
sentences.zh: 如果你换成天然色素，你可能不得不，第一，更换包装。

sentences.en: You know, you may not be able to have a clear bottle because now you're going to expose that natural color to light.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可能不能用透明瓶子了，因为现在你要把天然色素暴露在光线下。

sentences.en: The greens or the blues may separate.
sentences.zh: 绿色或蓝色可能会分离。

sentences.en: So when you pick that off the shelf, maybe the top of it is clear, but the bottom is where you've got your color sentiment now.
sentences.zh: 所以当你把它从货架上拿下来时，也许顶部是清澈的，但底部现在积聚了色素。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 哎呀。

sentences.en: And then on top of that, It also is going to change your manufacturing processes for these companies.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，这也将改变这些公司的制造工艺。

sentences.en: You know, artificial dyes can sit in tanks for weeks, years.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人工染料可以在罐子里放几个星期、几年。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: You know, they're fine.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们没问题。

sentences.en: But when you start to deal with natural colors, now you may have to refrigerate that.
sentences.zh: 但当你开始处理天然色素时，现在你可能得冷藏它。

sentences.en: And in order to achieve anything close to the colors that we've sort of achieved with artificial colors,
sentences.zh: 为了达到接近我们用人工色素所取得的颜色效果，

sentences.en: you may have to use 10 times the amount of carrot juice or beet juice to get the colors that you want.
sentences.zh: 你可能得用十倍剂量的胡萝卜汁或甜菜汁来获得想要的颜色。

sentences.en: You may have to reformulate your Lucky Charms or your Fruit Loops in terms of just the actual ingredients if you start to add these different colors to it.
sentences.zh: 如果你开始往里添加这些不同的颜色，你可能不得不重新配制你的幸运麦圈或水果圈麦片里实际的配料。

sentences.en: This is just much more complex than I think I could have possibly imagined before you just laid that out.
sentences.zh: 这比我想象的要复杂得多，在你刚才解释之前我根本想不到。

sentences.en: And I have to say I am personally disturbed and saddened to learn that a cool blue Gatorade doesn't occur naturally in our world.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，得知酷爽蓝佳得乐在我们的世界上并非天然存在，我个人感到很不安也很难过。

sentences.en: It sounds like companies also don't want to do it because they say it also increases our coSt.
sentences.zh: 听起来公司也不想这么做，因为他们说这也增加了我们的成本。

sentences.en: So there's this like one-two punch.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比是组合拳。

sentences.en: Fewer sales, higher costs.
sentences.zh: 销量下降，成本上升。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And all of this is coming at a really tough time for big food.
sentences.zh: 而所有这一切都发生在大食品公司一段非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: Almost across the board, you've seen volumes of their cookies and their chips decline.
sentences.zh: 几乎全面来看，你都能看到它们的曲奇和薯片的销量在下降。

sentences.en: I think after about two years of food inflation, you know, there's a lot of Americans that are just
sentences.zh: 我想在经历了大约两年的食品通胀之后，你知道的，很多美国人

sentences.en: either buying less of what they were buying before from these big food brands, or in some cases,
sentences.zh: 要么买这些大食品品牌的产品比以前少了，或者在某些情况下，

sentences.en: they're increasingly trading down to private label store brands, you know, the less expensive versions of those foods.
sentences.zh: 他们越来越多地转向购买平价的商店自有品牌，也就是那些价格更便宜的食品。

sentences.en: You know, on top of that, we also are seeing the fallout.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，除此之外，我们也看到了余波。

sentences.en: I think it's still early, but everybody's watching the rise of these weight loss drugs.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在还为时过早，但每个人都在关注这些减肥药的崛起。

sentences.en: You know, you're in Zempex, your GLP-1s, and there's lots of research behind that that says when Americans or people go on to
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如西马鲁肽、GLP-1受体激动剂，有很多研究表明，当美国人或人们使用

sentences.en: those drugs, they definitely eat less of these processed foods.
sentences.zh: 这些药物时，他们确实会减少吃这些加工食品。

sentences.en: And so food companies are looking at these big changes around their ingredients at a time when they're just also seeing sales and volumes of their foods falling off.
sentences.zh: 因此，食品公司正面临着这些围绕配料的巨大变革，与此同时，他们也看到自己食品的销量和出货量在下滑。

sentences.en: Okay, so these are the forces that RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪上任时要应对的力量，这个强大的食品行业几乎没有改变的动力，还有一个赋予公司相当大权力的监管环境。

sentences.en: is contending with when he comes into office, this powerful food industry with little incentive to change, a regulatory environment that gives companies quite a bit of power.
sentences.zh: 那么，肯尼迪上任不到一年，怎么就能真正有效地对抗这些势力呢？

sentences.en: So how is it that Kennedy, less than a year in office, has been able to actually effectively fight these forces?
sentences.zh: 为了对付大食品公司，你知道的，他某种程度上知道自己不能按常规套路出牌，对吧？

sentences.en: To go after big food, you know, he sort of knew he couldn't use the usual playbook, right?
sentences.zh: 监管，对吧？

sentences.en: Regulation, right?
sentences.zh: 制定规则，让每个人都来发表意见，包括食品公司和游说者。

sentences.en: Creating a rule, having everybody weigh in on it, including food companies and lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 这将会演变成一场“我的科学”对阵“你的科学”的大战，最后很可能会闹上法庭。

sentences.en: It would have gone down in sort of a big battle of my science versus your science, likely would have ended up in court.
sentences.zh: 他早就出局了。

sentences.en: He'd be gone.
sentences.zh: 什么改变都不会发生。

sentences.en: No change would happen.
sentences.zh: 所以为了真正促成改变，他决定采取一种非常新颖的方法。

sentences.en: So in order to really get change to occur here, he decided to take a very novel approach.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜·露。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.

sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天创作“拼字蜜蜂”和“字母包围”游戏。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazurski, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.zh: 想出了这个新颖的方法，让食品公司最终从他们的产品中剔除人工食用色素。

sentences.en: had come up with this novel approach to get food companies to finally eliminate artificial food dyes from their products.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个策略。

sentences.en: Tell me about that strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以他做的是对人工染料采取了一种更接近同业施压的监管方式。

sentences.en: So what he did was take much more of sort of a peer pressure approach to regulation on artificial dyes.
sentences.zh: 在四月份，他发布了一项声明，基本上是说我们将禁止某些染料，即美国食品系统中广泛使用的流行染料。

sentences.en: In April, he puts out an announcement basically saying that we're going to be banning certain dyes, popular dyes that are widely used in the American food system.
sentences.zh: 他召开了这场新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And he holds this press conference.
sentences.zh: 让我们欢迎他，美国儿童的斗士，小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪。

sentences.en: Let's join me in welcoming him, a warrior for America's children, RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当肯尼迪走上舞台时……

sentences.en: You know, when Kennedy comes up on stage...
sentences.zh: 我曾与我的员工讨论过这些石油基染料，我说，如果他们想吃石油，他们应该自己在家里添加。

sentences.en: I was talking with my staff about these petroleum-based dyes, and I said, if they want to eat petroleum, they ought to add it themselves at home.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该把它喂给我们其他人。

sentences.en: They shouldn't be feeding it to the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 他和台上的其他医疗领袖阐述了将人工染料清除出我们食品系统的计划。

sentences.en: And he and other health care leaders on stage lay out the plan to get artificial dyes out of our food system.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢食品公司与我们合作达成这一协议或和解。

sentences.en: And I want to commend the food companies for working with us to achieve this agreement or this settlement.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们说他们已经让所有这些公司加入了进来，但缺少的是什么呢，你知道的，没有哪个食品公司在场。

sentences.en: You know, they say they've got all these companies on board, but what's missing, you know, who's not there are any food companies.
sentences.zh: 这不是很奇怪吗？

sentences.en: And is that weird?
sentences.zh: 真的很奇怪。

sentences.en: It's really weird.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一个重大的声明，通常情况下，你会有，你知道的，几位公司高管站在那里对着镜头微笑着握手

sentences.en: You know, this is a big announcement, and it's normally something that you would have, you know, a few company executives up there smiling for the cameras and shaking hands
sentences.zh: 并表明他们支持这一愿景。

sentences.en: and showing that they're on board with this scene.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要回答记者的一些提问。

sentences.en: Today we're going to take some questions from the press.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你确实看到一个记者，有记者注意到现场没有食品公司的人，于是他们问肯尼迪。

sentences.en: You know, you actually see a reporter, and there's reporters that notice that there's no food companies that are there, and they ask Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 你提到目标是与食品行业合作，剔除大部分主要的合成食用色素。

sentences.en: You mentioned the goal is to work with the food industry to get most of the major synthetic food dyes out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如说，食品公司真的同意这样做吗？

sentences.en: You know, like, are the food companies really okay with this?
sentences.zh: 你们达成了什么样的协议？

sentences.en: What sort of agreements do you have?
sentences.zh: 如果食品行业不同意自愿这样做，计划是什么？

sentences.en: What is the plan if the food industry does not voluntarily agree to do that?
sentences.zh: 如果你无法在业内达成协议，接下来的步骤是什么？

sentences.en: And what are the next steps if you can't get agreement within the industry?
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他说，是的，我们达成了这种共识。

sentences.en: And basically, he says, yeah, we have this understanding.
sentences.zh: 这正在发生。

sentences.en: It's happening.
sentences.zh: 我们将与这个行业合作。

sentences.en: We are going to work with the industry.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面表现出了很大的领导力。

sentences.en: They've shown a lot of leadership on this.
sentences.zh: 他说他们已经加入了。

sentences.en: He says they are on board.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 他们真的加入了？

sentences.en: And are they?
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 幕后发生了什么？

sentences.en: What's happening behind the scenes?
sentences.zh: 我在声明发布后不久与一位接近政府的人士交谈过。

sentences.en: I spoke with a person close to the administration shortly after the announcement.
sentences.zh: 基本上他们得到的是一家公司的口头初步协议。

sentences.en: and basically what they had was a soft agreement from one company.
sentences.zh: 哇，一家公司的初步协议并不等于所有人都在背后支持这一点。

sentences.en: Wow, a soft agreement from one company is not everyone is lined up behind this.
sentences.zh: 所以小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪

sentences.en: So did RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 只是在虚张声势吗？

sentences.en: just bluff?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他在虚张声势。

sentences.en: He bluffed.
sentences.zh: 他所希望的，或者说孤注一掷的是，行业中的这家公司——他们没有透露是谁——但他们预计会发表声明

sentences.en: And what he hoped was, or was sort of banking on, was that this one company in the industry, they would not say who it was, but that they expected an announcement to be made
sentences.zh: 在记者会后几周内，这将成为整个行业开始崩塌的开始。

sentences.en: within a couple of weeks of the press conference and that that would be the beginning of sort of the whole industry toppling over.

sentences.en: And it seems like his bet on that domino effect happening actually paid off.
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么发展的？

sentences.en: How did that exactly go down?
sentences.zh: 从百事公司开始，它生产多力多滋、奇多和所有这些受欢迎的零食。

sentences.en: It starts with PepsiCo, which makes Doritos and Cheetos and all these popular snacks.

sentences.en: And the executives mentioned that they're going to start to move a number of their chips.

sentences.en: Lay's chips are going to have no artificial colors in them by the end of this year.

sentences.en: And then you get to like June and Kraft Heinz comes out and they say, we are going to be rid of artificial dyes in our foods and beverages and whatever by the end of 2027.

sentences.en: More companies, you know, Nestle, General Mills, Smuckers, W.K.
sentences.zh: 家乐氏，也就是水果圈的制造商，其麦片也表示，将在2027年底前在其食品、麦片和产品中停用人工色素。

sentences.en: Kellogg, which is Fruit Loops, which is these cereals that says it too will be out of artificial colors in its foods and cereals and products by the end of 2027.
sentences.zh: 我只是对你所描述的食品公司宣布愿意改变的雪崩般、级联般的声浪感到震惊。

sentences.en: I'm just struck by the avalanche, the cascade you described of announcements of these food companies saying, we are willing to change.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 如果他们回应的事情实际上只是小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的软实力，他们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Why are they doing this if the thing they're responding to is really just soft power on the part of RFK Jr.?
sentences.zh: 这是软实力，但这也是权力。

sentences.en: It's soft power, but it's power.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一届政府比过去的政府更能引起人们的恐惧，对吧？

sentences.en: And I think this administration, more so than past administrations causes a lot of fear, right?
sentences.zh: 你已经看到了，如果他们不喜欢你在做的事情，他们可以雷霆出击，让你的日子变得非常、非常难过。

sentences.en: You've seen where if they don't like something you're doing, they can come down and they can make your life really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 我认为食品行业有一种心态，那就是，好吧，人工染料。

sentences.en: And I think there's an element of the food industry saying, okay, artificial dyes.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢它。

sentences.en: We don't like it.
sentences.zh: 这会花我们的钱，也许我们会改，也许我们不会改。

sentences.en: It's going to cost us money and maybe we will, maybe we won't change.
sentences.zh: 我们走着瞧吧。

sentences.en: We'll see how that plays out.
sentences.zh: 但如果这能让他们高兴，我们就说我们要改变它，希望他们能放过我们，因为这里还有其他更大的博弈或更重要的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: But if it makes them happy, we say we're going to change it and hopefully they leave us alone because there's other like sort of like big game here or bigger issues, right?
sentences.zh: 如果这届政府出来说少糖、少脂、少盐，那真的会让这个行业陷入恶性循环。

sentences.en: If this administration comes out and says less sugar, less fat, less salt, that will really throw this industry into, you know, a downward spiral.
sentences.zh: 那比从这些东西中去除染料还要困难。

sentences.en: That's even harder than dyes to remove from this stuff.
sentences.zh: 困难得多，而且绝对会影响销量，你知道的。

sentences.en: Much more difficult and would absolutely impact sales, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有一点点成分，我认为，就像是，安抚这届政府，给他们一场胜利，

sentences.en: So there's a little bit of an element here of, I think, like, pacify this administration, give them a win,
sentences.zh: 并希望在接下来的几年里能大大地低调行事。

sentences.en: and hope that you can fly below the radar for the next few years in a big way.
sentences.zh: 不过说到你的观点，我不得不想象这个策略的一个缺陷是，这里显然没有任何新的法规。

sentences.en: To your point, though, I have to imagine that one pitfall of this strategy is that there are no new regulations here, obviously.
sentences.zh: 小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪

sentences.en: RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 空手套白狼。

sentences.en: is just relying on his own persuasive power or perhaps the company's not wanting to get on the wrong side of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 仅仅依赖他自身的说服力，或者也许是这家公司不想得罪特朗普政府。

sentences.en: But that means this push doesn't actually have any real teeth.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着这项推动实际上没有任何真正的约束力。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And definitely skeptics or critics will note this industry said and looked into making these changes a decade ago, and many of them didn't.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无疑问，怀疑论者或批评者会指出，这个行业在十年前就说过并研究过要做出这些改变，但他们中的许多人并没有这样做。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, so there's definitely a group of people that worry that we could get to the end of 2027, and most of our major food and beverages and snacks still contain artificial
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以肯定有一群人担心，当我们走到2027年底时，我们的大多数主要食品、饮料和零食仍然含有造假

sentences.en: colors.
sentences.zh: 色素。

sentences.en: But that's where, for the industry, though, there's another aspect of this,
sentences.zh: 但对这个行业来说，这里还有另一个方面，

sentences.en: which is the emerging state laws that could actually be a bigger problem for them.
sentences.zh: 那就是正在涌现的州法律，这实际上可能对他们来说是一个更大的问题。

sentences.en: What are those state laws?
sentences.zh: 这些州法律是什么？

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个。

sentences.en: So you've got a number of states, including California, Texas, West Virginia, that are
sentences.zh: 所以你有许多州，包括加利福尼亚州、得克萨斯州、西弗吉尼亚州，它们

sentences.en: actually creating laws around artificial colors that are much more stringent, that are actual, you know, in some cases, bans.
sentences.zh: 实际上正在围绕人工色素制定更加严格的法律，在某些情况下，这些法律实际上就是禁令。

sentences.en: In other cases, Texas wants warning labels.
sentences.zh: 在其他情况下，得克萨斯州希望贴上警告标签。

sentences.en: They're creating a set of rules for the food industry that's going to cause it significant problems because, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们正在为食品行业制定一套规则，这将给她带来重大问题，因为，你知道的，

sentences.en: the industry is very much worried about a patchwork quilt of rules, as they like to say.
sentences.zh: 正如他们喜欢说的那样，这个行业非常担心规则会变得像百衲被一样零碎杂乱。

sentences.en: If you are
sentences.zh: 如果你是

sentences.en: M&M Mars.
sentences.zh: M&M玛氏。

sentences.en: Now, if you're making your candy and you're selling it in Texas, you're going to have to have a warning label, but not in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你在制作糖果并将其在得克萨斯州销售，你将不得不贴上警告标签，但在新墨西哥州则不用。

sentences.en: You know, it's really difficult and confusing for them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对他们来说真的很难，而且很混乱。

sentences.en: But those are actual rules that could create more change than this administration can with this voluntary movement.
sentences.zh: 但这些都是实际的规则，比起本届政府通过这场自愿运动，它们可能会带来更多的改变。

sentences.en: The fact that it's Texas and like West Virginia that's doing this, adding regulations on this stuff, is surprising.
sentences.zh: 事实上是得克萨斯州和西弗吉尼亚州这样在做，在这个问题上增加监管，这令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I mean, those are red states and not places that I would necessarily expect to be leading the pack on food regulation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是红州，并不是我原本预期会在食品监管方面走在前列的地方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, you have California, you know, a much more liberal left-leaning state, which has been ahead of all of this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，你有加利福尼亚州，你知道的，一个更加自由派、倾向左翼的州，它一直走在所有这些的前面。

sentences.en: But it also shows, I think, the power, the political power of the Maha movement, that you have Texas, that you have West Virginia, you know, sort of these
sentences.zh: 但这也表明，我认为，马哈运动的力量，即政治力量，你有得克萨斯州，你有西弗吉尼亚州，你知道的，基本上这些

sentences.en: deep red states that are basically saying, we're going to regulate artificial dyes in a way that the federal government is not doing.
sentences.zh: 深红州正在表示，我们将以联邦政府没有做的方式来监管人工色素。

sentences.en: I want to step back here for a minute and just ask what you think RFK is really up to here.
sentences.zh: 我想在这里退一步，简单问一下你认为小肯尼迪在这里到底在搞什么名堂。

sentences.en: I think it's clear he's trying to bypass the bureaucracy, force companies with the soft power to make these pretty radical changes to the way our food looks.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，他正试图绕过官僚机构，用软实力迫使公司对我们食物外观做出这些相当激进的改变。

sentences.en: But even if he does succeed, if you make Froot Loops less colorful, less neon, maybe you on the margins do some good if the research is right.
sentences.zh: 但即使他成功了，如果你让彩虹糖（Froot Loops）颜色没那么丰富、没那么荧光，如果研究是对的话，也许你在边缘上做了一些好事。

sentences.en: But are you fundamentally changing the big health issues that he and other people care about?
sentences.zh: 但你从根本上改变了他和其他人关心的重大健康问题了吗？

sentences.en: So if you talk to nutritionists, you know, or health experts, you know, they're sort of one
sentences.zh: 所以如果你和营养学家谈谈，你知道的，或者健康专家，你知道的，他们某种程度上是

sentences.en: of their biggest criticism of going after food dyes, there's a little bit of a so-what-ism here, right?
sentences.zh: 他们对追查食用色素的最大批评之一，这里有点“那又怎样”的意味，对吧？

sentences.en: There's really no studies that say food dyes equals obesity, food dyes equals diabetes, right?
sentences.zh: 真的没有任何研究表明食用色素等于肥胖，食用色素等于糖尿病，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's sort of like, great, fine, you get that out of the system, but it's not really attacking your core mission statement, which is that chronic disease.
sentences.zh: 所以有点像是，太好了，很好，你把那个从系统中清理出去了，但这并没有真正攻击你的核心使命，也就是那些慢性病。

sentences.en: But then there's another sort of line of thinking around all of this is whether in making these foods and snacks and drinks less pretty, less bright,
sentences.zh: 但随后还有另一种思路，围绕着这一切，就是在让这些食品、零食和饮料看起来没那么好看、没那么鲜艳的过程中，

sentences.en: are you in a roundabout way tackling the bigger issue, which is the chronic disease, which is the obesity, which is the diabetes.
sentences.zh: 你是否在以一种迂回的方式解决更大的问题，也就是慢性病，也就是肥胖症，也就是糖尿病。

sentences.en: And especially when we're talking about children.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当我们谈论儿童的时候。

sentences.en: If children who were drawn to brightly colored cereals and consuming boxes of them, you know, now eat less or eat smaller portion sizes of them,
sentences.zh: 如果那些被颜色鲜艳的谷物吸引并吃掉一盒又一盒的儿童，你知道的，现在吃得少了，或者吃的份量变小了，

sentences.en: are you now tackling the bigger issue around sugar, salt, saturated fat, portion control?
sentences.zh: 你现在是不是在解决围绕糖、盐、饱和脂肪、份量控制的更大问题？

sentences.en: You know, we're really talking about retraining America, retraining the American mindset, the connection between our eyes and our palate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们实际上是在谈论重新训练美国，重新训练美国人的思维方式，我们眼睛和味蕾之间的联系。

sentences.en: And, you know, if we say, I don't want this, I'm going to eat less of this, that could be a win.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果我们说，我不想要这个，我要少吃这个，那可能会是一场胜利。

sentences.en: That could absolutely be a win in terms of our overall intake of ultra processed foods.
sentences.zh: 就我们总体摄入超加工食品而言，这绝对可能是一场胜利。

sentences.en: Julie, thank you.
sentences.zh: 朱莉，谢谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感谢你抽空接受采访。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: On Sunday afternoon, President Trump announced that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周日下午，特朗普总统宣布美国

sentences.en: and the European Union had reached a trade deal, setting a 15 percent tariff on most goods, including cars.
sentences.zh: 与欧盟达成了一项贸易协议，对包括汽车在内的多数商品征收15%的关税。

sentences.en: The agreement is in line with a deal that Trump recently reached with Japan,
sentences.zh: 该协议与特朗普最近和日本达成的协议一致，

sentences.en: and it brought an end to months of tense negotiations with some of America's closest allies and trading partners.
sentences.zh: 它结束了与美国一些最亲密的盟友和贸易伙伴几个月来紧张的谈判。

sentences.en: But the new rate was a big increase from tariffs that had previously been in place and was much higher than Europe had been pushing for.
sentences.zh: 但新税率比之前实施的关税大幅增加，并且远高于欧洲一直在争取的目标。

sentences.en: And Israel said that it paused military activity in parts of Gaza on Sunday to allow international aid in as outrage grows over the severe hunger
sentences.zh: 以色列表示，周日暂停了加沙部分地区的军事活动，以允许国际援助物资进入，因为人们对飞地内巴勒斯坦人面临的严重饥饿

sentences.en: facing Palestinians in the enclave.
sentences.zh: 的愤怒情绪日益高涨。

sentences.en: Israeli forces suspended operations in at least three areas of Gaza and plan to designate secure routes for the United Nations to deliver aid, according to the Israeli military.
sentences.zh: 据以色列军方称，以色列军队暂停了加沙至少三个地区的行动，并计划为联合国运送援助物资指定安全路线。

sentences.en: The U.N.
sentences.zh: 联合国

sentences.en: says more than one in three people in Gaza has not been eating for multiple days in a row.
sentences.zh: 表示，加沙超过三分之一的人连续几天没有吃过东西。

sentences.en: And according to Gaza's health ministry, more than 50 Palestinians have died this month from starvation.
sentences.zh: 根据加沙卫生部的消息，本月已有50多名巴勒斯坦人死于饥饿。
